texts.facts: This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident. 2. The brief facts of the case are as follows: On 23-07-2021 at about 7.00 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding on the scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EQ-0492 from Chandapura, on Sarjapura-Bengaluru main road, infront of Chambenahalli Gate, as a pillion rider, being ridden by its rider carefully, cautiously, by following all the traffic rules and regulations. At that time, a Toyota Innova car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-MY-5409, driven by its driver with high speed, in rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, came from behind and dashed against the scooter bearing Reg. No.TN-24-AB-3750 and then to the scooter of the petitioner. Due to the said impact, the petitioner has fell down and Sathyendra vs Raghavendra H.M on 27 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118684947/ 2 sustained grievous injuries all over the body. Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Columbia Asia Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient. Earlier to the accident he was working as painter and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month. But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity. The Sarjapura Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said car, for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of IPC. The respondent No.1 is the driver, respondent No.2 is the owner and respondent No.3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle. Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest. 3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 to 3 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements. 4. The respondents No.1 and 2 in their written statement have denied all the allegations made in the petition. They have contended that, as on the date of alleged accident, the Toyota Innova car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-MY-5409 was having valid insurance with the respondent No.3 insurance company, bundled long term liability policy vide policy No.991491823740007118, valid from 15-10-2020 to 14-10- 2021. Further they have contended that, as on the date of accident, the driver of said car was having valid and effective driving licence to drive the same. Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition against them. 5. The respondent No.3 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition. It has admitted the issuance of private car/third party liability only policy bearing No.991401823740007118 in favour of respondent No.2, in respect of car bearing Reg. No.KA-05- MY-5409 and it was valid from 15-10-2018 to 14-10-2021 and it was valid as on the date of accident. It has contended that, the petition is bad for non-compliance of provisions under Section 134(c) of Motor Vehicles Act. They are the proper and necessary parties to the above proceedings to adjudicate the controversy involved between the parties in the above matter. It has denied the occurrence, mode of the accident and also involvement of the vehicle bearing No.KA-05-MY- 5409 as alleged in the claim petition. For the above stated denials and contentions, it is prayed for dismiss the petition. 6. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed: ISSUES 1. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 17 documents as Ex.P.1 to 17. Further, he has got examined one more witness namely Dr. S. Ramachandra as P.W.2. On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has examined himself as R.W.1 and got marked 3 documents as Ex.R.1 to 3. Due to the said impact, the petitioner has fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated entire averments made in the petition.
texts.arguments: Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties, the owner and insurer of motorcycle bearing No.KA-53-EQ- 0492 which involved in the alleged accident are not made as parties to the above proceedings. Further it is contended that, the respondent No.2 had willfully entrusted his vehicle to a person who did not possess valid and effective driving licence to drive the same, as on the date of accident. It is clear breach of terms and conditions of the policy and also violation of Section 149(2) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988. Further it is contended that, the alleged accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EQ-0492, on which the petitioner was the pillion rider. The rider and pillion riders who were not wearing safety headgear, was not holding driving licence to ride the said motorcycle and insurance to use the said vehicle on the public road. It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses and treatment taken by him. Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant. Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2 under Sathyendra vs Raghavendra H.M on 27 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118684947/ 3 Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act. Further, the respondent No.3 has taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EQ-0492, on which the petitioner was a pillion rider and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-MY-5409. On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Toyota Innova car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-MY- 5409 and dashing the same to the scooter bearing Reg. from behind and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries all over the body in the said accident. Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.3 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EQ-0492 or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) 11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required." 17. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be Sathyendra vs Raghavendra H.M on 27 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118684947/ 6 applied."
